touches.text: Logging and diagnostics, including diagnostic_inspector: the smart reader of the dumb breadcrumbs base's logging leaves; complete diagnosis on the first pass.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".

conflicts.text: The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#98, following Akien's answer to Q#90.
conflicts.ticket_says: exit non-zero (red) on platforms without systemctl or /proc
conflicts.why: Outline 9.4.8.1 states 'A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's', using absolute language 'never red'. The ticket proposes a non-zero exit (red exit code) as interim behavior until the NOTRUN mechanism is implemented. These directly contradict: the outline says tests on unsupported platforms should yield NOTRUN outcomes, never red, while the ticket proposes red. The ticket acknowledges this is interim ('a follow-up turns the line into NOTRUN') but the two proposals differ immediately.
